title: Small Simple Steps
coreMove: Lower the entry cost until the next visible action can happen now.
sourcePressure: The motivation formula becomes behavioral by shrinking the first move so action can begin with less resistance.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: Confusing a small start with making the whole goal trivial.
sourceAnchorNote: Frozen sidecar contains no chapter-local named figure, named study, named place, or dated anecdote. Use fictional protagonists and keep source alignment at the concept and title-pressure level.

hook: Do not open Small Simple Steps with a generic unlocked potential claim.
Do not start with a definition of small simple steps.
counterintuition: Do not use a not X but Y correction shell.
Do not claim the opposite of common sense in generic coaching language.
tryThisNow: Do not use set a timer and reflect.
Do not ask the reader to journal broadly without a visible action.
examples: No repeated desk, kitchen, classroom, commute, or generic meeting shells.
No six examples built around timestamp plus named protagonist plus decision.

exampleOpeningDiversity.rule: no more than 2 of the 6 examples may open with the pattern 'At HH:MM, <Name> <verb>s'
exampleOpeningDiversity.requiredOpenings: at least 4 distinct opening devices across the 6 examples, drawn from: timestamp+name+action, dialogue first line, sensory detail first, second-person You direct address, retrospective It took her three weeks to see, question-as-hook, environmental detail before any human
exampleOpeningDiversity.rationale: C8 catches Cartesian repetition of phrases but not the deeper template of 'timestamp + named protagonist + prop + decision' that makes 6 examples feel like 1 example with name swaps

exampleSpecs.audience: executor avoiding a full box of forms
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Rebecca chooses only the envelope labeled bank statements and places it on the scanner before touching the rest of the box.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: one cream envelope on a flatbed scanner

exampleSpecs.audience: line cook intimidated by a full new menu
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Julien reduces the task to one garnish cut, lays out five radishes, and completes the first clean set before reading another recipe.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: five radishes beside a chef knife

exampleSpecs.stakes: ballots mail out in ten days
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Isabel writes one street and knocks on the first blue door instead of designing the whole campaign again.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a blue door with a taped campaign flyer

exampleSpecs.audience: tenant wants lower bills but avoids the whole apartment checklist
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Niklas installs one door sweep before pricing windows, proving the first move can be smaller than the entire problem.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a rolled rubber door sweep on the floor

exampleSpecs.audience: mentor helping a shy student start a game project
exampleSpecs.stakes: demo day is close and the blank editor is freezing her
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Adaeze asks for one sprite movement, not a whole game, and watches the first arrow key move a square.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a blank editor with one green square

exampleSpecs.stakes: rent depends on collecting two overdue payments
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: James sees that progress began when he opened only the oldest invoice and wrote the first subject line.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: an overdue invoice highlighted in pale blue

rhythmVariety.deepReadParagraphLengthMix: at least one paragraph 3 sentences or shorter, at least one paragraph 5+ sentences, at least one one-sentence punch line
rhythmVariety.fullReadInterludeRequirement: at least one paragraph that breaks the scene-then-rule rhythm, using a question to the reader, a research aside only if source-supported, a direct second-person passage, or a brief historical reference
rhythmVariety.forbiddenRhythm: every paragraph following the pattern 'concrete anchor sentence -> abstract rule sentence -> elaboration sentence'

skillTargets: Identify when lower the entry cost until the next visible action can happen now. is needed in a new scenario.
Choose the visible action that matches Small Simple Steps rather than a nearby generic lesson.
Explain why the weak alternative fails without using recall-only phrasing.

tryThisNowSpec: Shrink the next task until it can be done with one object already in reach.
